info.name: Pagination Contract Lab
info.description: Six primary pagination contract scenarios for the local synthetic-products API. Each folder starts with an independently executable primary request. Test 5 includes seven supplementary validation requests; Test 6 includes the supplementary over-limit request. Collection-level scripts check JSON structure, product fields, unique IDs, and error codes. Request-level scripts check scenario-specific status, counts, slicing, and metadata. No requests depend on earlier requests or stored responses. No saved response examples are included. Run against the local server, then capture actual evidence. See docs/API_CONTRACT.md and docs/TEST_PLAN.md.

item.name: Test 1 — Default pagination
item.description: Confirm omitted parameters independently default to page 1 and limit 10.

request.description: Purpose: verify the default first page. No query parameters. Expected: HTTP 200, prod-001 through prod-010, 23 total items, 3 total pages, next=true, previous=false.

exec: pm.test('T1: HTTP 200, default page, count, and metadata', function () {
pm.expect(body.pagination).to.deep.equal({ page: 1, limit: 10, totalItems: 23, totalPages: 3, hasNextPage: true, hasPreviousPage: false });
pm.expect(body.data.map(function (product) { return product.id; })).to.deep.equal(Array.from({ length: 10 }, function (_, index) { return 'prod-' + String(index + 1).padStart(3, '0'); }));

item.name: Test 5 — Invalid pagination inputs
item.description: The primary request has two invalid fields; its single error cannot prove each field is validated independently. Supplementary requests isolate negative page, zero limit, fractional page/limit, nonnumeric page/limit, and an unknown query key. All must return HTTP 400 with the documented error code and message.

item.name: T5 Primary — Invalid page and limit

request.description: Purpose: verify invalid pagination returns HTTP 400, not defaulted data. Query: page=0, limit=-1. Expected: INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER and the page message, because page validation is reported first. Supplementary requests isolate each invalid-field category.

exec: pm.test('T5: HTTP 400 and the documented first-field validation message', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.deep.equal({ error: { code: 'INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER', message: 'The page must be an integer between 1 and 9007199254740991.' } });

request.description: Purpose: isolate a negative page with a valid limit. Expected: HTTP 400 and the page validation error.

exec: pm.test('T5a: negative page returns HTTP 400 with the page error', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.deep.equal({ error: { code: 'INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER', message: 'The page must be an integer between 1 and 9007199254740991.' } });

request.description: Purpose: isolate limit=0 with a valid page. Expected: HTTP 400 and the limit validation error.

exec: pm.test('T5b: zero limit returns HTTP 400 with the limit error', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.deep.equal({ error: { code: 'INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER', message: 'The limit must be an integer between 1 and 20.' } });

item.name: Test 6 — Maximum page-size enforcement
item.description: Check both sides of the limit boundary in separate independently executable requests: 20 is accepted, 21 is rejected. Both results are required to mark this scenario Pass.

request.description: Purpose: accept the exact maximum page size. Query: page=1, limit=20. Expected: HTTP 200, prod-001 through prod-020, 20 unique products, totalItems=23, totalPages=2, next=true, previous=false. Also run T6a to verify rejection above the maximum.

exec: pm.test('T6: HTTP 200, maximum-size page, stable IDs, and exact metadata', function () {
pm.expect(body.pagination).to.deep.equal({ page: 1, limit: 20, totalItems: 23, totalPages: 2, hasNextPage: true, hasPreviousPage: false });
pm.expect(body.data.map(function (product) { return product.id; })).to.deep.equal(Array.from({ length: 20 }, function (_, index) { return 'prod-' + String(index + 1).padStart(3, '0'); }));

request.description: Purpose: enforce the upper boundary without clamping. Query: page=1, limit=21. Expected: HTTP 400, INVALID_QUERY_PARAMETER, and the documented limit message.

exec: pm.test('T6a: limit=21 returns HTTP 400, not a clamped page', function () {
